Subject: Scheduling: On‑Prem Architecture Review & Constraints (LongView Health)

Hi Jorge — thanks again for the discovery call earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- We heard LongView needs a private/on‑prem proof-of-concept to evaluate integration, network egress controls, and data residency constraints.
- Key decision criteria you flagged: encryption at rest in customer KMS, isolated VPC peering, and audited access logs (S3 + audit trail).

Proposed next step: 60‑minute technical architecture review with our Private Deploy lead and an infra engineer. Goal: align on network topology, security constraints, and a realistic slot for a PoC.

Possible agenda (30/60 min):
- 5m intros and objectives
- 15m LongView constraints & compliance checklist (you)
- 25m Redwood architecture options & tradeoffs (our infra lead)
- 15m Action items / PoC plan / timelines

Can you confirm who from your side should attend (network/security, SRE, procurement)? Also posting a couple of slot options below — if none work, propose two times that do.

Slot options (PST):
- Tue 23 Feb, 10:00–11:00 PST
- Wed 24 Feb, 15:00–16:00 PST

Attachments: LVH_PoC_PreRead.pdf (short checklist + sample VPC diagrams). I'll share a Drive folder after we lock time.

Thanks,
Connor

Connor — thanks for the recap and the clear agenda.

Realistically, we need these people on the call: Ana Patel (SRE), Miguel Santos (Network/Security), and our procurement lead, Dana Lee. Can you accommodate them? Also two quick asks before we meet: 

1) Can Redwood confirm you support customer KMS integration (we use AWS KMS with external key rotation policy)?
2) Please send any standard SOC2 documentation or a pointer to your security pack ahead of time. Procurement wants that flagged before a PoC.

For timing, Wed 24 Feb 15:00–16:00 PST works best for the SRE team. If you can send a calendar invite for that slot, I'll loop in the attendees.

On the PoC scope: we want a minimal exposure deployment (no internet egress from model nodes; only allowed egress to our telemetry collector and S3 in our account). Will Redwood be able to support that pattern?

Thanks,
Jorge Ramos

Thanks Jorge — Wed 24 Feb 15:00–16:00 PST is blocked on our side and we'll send a calendar invite shortly.

Quick answers to your asks: 
- KMS: yes — we support AWS KMS customer‑managed keys and can document the key lifecycle and rotation approach. We'll include a short diagram of where the CMK is applied in the deployment.
- SOC2 / Security pack: attaching a link stub to our security pack (see dataroom link below) and I'll ask Marissa to follow up with the SOC2 summary PDF.

Regarding the egress constraint: we can run the model nodes in a private subnet with no outbound internet egress. Allowed egress can be restricted to your telemetry collector IPs and an S3 bucket in your account via VPC endpoints — this is the recommended pattern for an on‑prem / VPC-isolated PoC. We'll surface the network diagram in the call and list firewall rules to pre-open.

Could you confirm the attendee list (Ana, Miguel, Dana) and whether the call should include any purchasing/procurement artifact owners? Also let us know if you prefer Zoom or your corporate Webex.

Attachments: redwood_priv_deploy_dataroom_link.txt (contains Drive + security pack pointers).

Connor
